What are you looking for in the Merlin? How strong of a fighter should it be? What sort of speed should it achieve? What are you afraid it may include that is different from the original pitch?

The snub fighter aspect tells me it should be quick, turn sharp on a dime, and have a decent 'default' armoury. Nothing OP, but certainly something a skilled pilot could comfortably take down a Hornet with.

Also really hope they don't shove a jump drive in there.

Forget a jump drive, I'm not sure it should have a Q-Drive. CIG have already said they aren't giving it a virtual HUD or its own radar. If it doesn't have room for those, it shouldn't have room for a jump drive.

The whole point of the Merlin is that it has to stay close to its mother Connie. I think that it should be a big gun strapped to a rocket that. It should be really nimble, it should hit really hard, and it should be out of fuel and ammo very, very quickly.

This. Yup. It's an emergency, there are two many to cope. Best pilot in the Merlin, blast as fast and hard as you can, thin the numbers.

True, maybe the Q drive should be axed too, if it exists. Would hardly be a short range snub if it could cross a sol system. I'm looking forward to seeing it perform in AC.

I really don't think it should be able to beat a Hornet easily. I think it'd be best as a gnat to harass fighters and get them to forget about the Constellation nearby. They fly right into the firing arc of the Connie, and are obliterated.

I agree, I see the merlin more as a utility or support craft to up the dps, make life generally difficult for attackers, decoy and draw pirates into firing arcs. Basically I see it being much more important to be maneuverable, but it still has to have a punch hard enough to make it tempting, and/or beneficial to attack.
And this will probably be a much used tactic, but flown by a really good pilot, really really good, I can envisage it being very frustrating to fly against.

I feel like it's so fragile that being merely a "gnat" to harass fighters would get it, and its pilot, blown up real quick.

Take down a hornet comfortably? Ummm... No.

Hornets are purpose built combat vessels. They fight. It's what they do. It's all that they do. The Merlin won't be able to compete with that.

Against an aurora? The balance should be towards the merlin, I reckon. Against a Mustang? That might be a more even fight.

Really? I don't know. I saw it as being a big, if only a very short lived, bang. But, then again I see what you mean. It will be a light fighter and pretty easily chewed up.

In the hands of a casual player? No doubt it will be a frustrating existence in Battle Royale. But with someone who can really fly? We'll see I guess
It should be really maneuverable, have low armour and very limited range. Speed should be moderate. It should be like a small version of the Gladius. Less weapons and armour.

This won't be popular, but I think the Merlin should have such a terrible power plant that after you do a full discharge of your M3A's you basically have to retreat to recharge them. (Which could be a cool gameplay mechanic of buzz and run)

It should be faster than an M50, more agile, but its shields and armor should be pitiful/non-existent.

Remember, this guy is backed up by the full force of a connie - and isn't the Arch or the M50. If they make this ship "good" then those other ships need to be FANTASTIC. I'd much rather they all be balanced... and the only way to balance this ship is to make it a glass cannon... or more appropriately a glass pistol.

It should win ~50% of the time against an Aurora. Against a Gladius or a Hornet it should only be able to win if those pilots are basically terrible.

And before anyone says every ship needs to be equal... remember that this is a snub fighter.

If the Merlin can hold its own against a Hornet or Gladius... then the UEE would have fleets of them instead.

I think there is a place for that kind of Merlin design, it is one side of spectrum and I wouldn't be surprised or diassapointed it that's how turns out in pu. I guess in AC they won't place such limitations on it, to provide proper testing.

Hello friend!

I'm actually going to be in Pitts for the first time next month.

Gonna be there all week last week of Aug, staying downtown.

Any good recommendations on bars I can go get mildly shitfaced at? Or restaurants?

Whereabouts will you be staying? The Southside has all the bars where most people get shitfaced. I like Piper's Pub but I stay away from the whole area during nights and weekends because it gets crowded and loud. You can walk up one side of the street and down the other and bar hop til your liver explodes. If you want to sample local brews we have Penn Brewery, Church Brew Works, Rivertowne and others. The best wings I've ever had are at Sidelines in Millvale. It's a little bit of a drive out of the city but not hard to get too. Usually a good selection of beers there and it's in my neck of the woods. If you want pure selection try the Sharp Edge Bistro or Sharp Edge Beer Emporium. I've been to the Emporium, which is fantastic. The Bistro is downtown, though, but I don't know if they keep the same selection of suds as the other.

Booked at the Pittsburgh Marriott City Center...

Thanks for the advice! I'll be there from Tues-Sunday, so should be able to soak up plenty of food/booze while I am there I think. I'm more of a dive-bar person anyway.

How's the local transit? Can I bus it? Or Uber? What's the preferred way? Is there anything Pitts is known for? Like Phillys in Philly..etc.

Thanks again for the knowledge! Let me know if you have a free night and want to get a pint!

The Marriott is a good location. Should be able to walk to just about anywhere. The Sharp Edge Bistro is a couple of blocks away. You can walk to the Strip District and get a Primanti's sandwich which is a Pittsburgh icon. Really, if you've never had one and visit Pittsburgh there's no reason you shouldn't get one and the one in the Strip District is the original.

You should go ahead and check out the fountain at Point State Park. That's where the three rivers meet. From there you can cross a bridge to the North Shore where the stadiums, casino and science center are. Cross the other river and you get to Station Square which looks like it's having some free concerts that week. Over there is where the incline is, as well, which will take you up to Mount Washington and has the best views of the city.

Really, if you get a Primanti's Sandwich, go to the Point, go up the incline and take a touristy picture of yourself with the city in the background you'll have had a pretty Pittsburghy trip. Everything else will be just gravy.

Our public transit is lacking but I've heard Uber is dropping rates in our area so that might be good for you.

If we find a day that works I'd love to grab a beer somewhere. Maybe be your tour guide for a bit!
